tagline: Prove what's actually fixed — and how long it took.
lore: The Plott, a hound that bays the moment it trees its quarry — here it trails the findings that have been fixed, so you can prove what is put to bed.
problem: Remediation is only real when the finding closes. Showing what was fixed, when, how long it took and whether it met SLA usually means stitching exports together.
does: Plott searches navi's remediation history: every fixed finding with each finding's first-seen and fixed dates, days to fix (computed, not trusted from navi's text field) and navi's own SLA Pass / Fail, SLA failures first.

glance.caption: Plott's results: each fixed finding with plugin, severity, first seen, fixed on, days to fix and its SLA verdict, worst first.

capabilities: every fixed finding with plugin, name, severity and state.
computed from first seen to fixed.
navi's own Pass / Fail, from navi's SLA calculation.
SLA failures first, then by severity; the asset opens Argos.
a question becomes one read-only SQL query over the remediation-history table that you can edit before it runs (needs an AI model).
export the rows or send them through Gabriel.
how: Plott reads the fixed table in your local navi.db (filled by `navi config update fixed`; navi's SLA calculation stamps each row Pass / Fail) and changes nothing.
who: VM leads proving progress, and auditors asking for remediation evidence.
better: Sköll measures SLA across open and fixed findings; Plott is the row-level proof behind it.
cta: Follow Plott's trail to what's really fixed — and how fast.
